## Purpose and execution model
This is a fork-and-customize Terraform blueprint for building a secure Google Cloud enterprise foundation. It is not an application: independent Terraform root projects must be applied in dependency order, first manually for bootstrap and then through CI/CD. The primary entry points are the numbered stage roots, especially `0-bootstrap/main.tf`, `1-org/envs/shared/`, and per-environment `main.tf` roots.

## 0. Bootstrap: state, identities, and deployment platform
`0-bootstrap/` establishes the prerequisite deployment boundary in an existing GCP organization: seed/state and CI/CD projects, Terraform service accounts, IAM, and the selected execution integration (Cloud Build by default; GitHub, GitLab, local, and Terraform Cloud examples exist).
- `0-bootstrap/main.tf`
- `0-bootstrap/build_cb.tf`
- `0-bootstrap/sa.tf`

It produces the credentials, remote state location, and pipeline resources consumed by later stages.

## 1. Organization baseline
The shared organization root creates top-level folders, foundational projects, organization IAM/policies, service controls, logging, SCC notification, and network-project scaffolding. It is the boundary between organization governance and environment-specific resources.
- `1-org/envs/shared/projects.tf`
- `1-org/envs/shared/org_policy.tf`
- `1-org/envs/shared/log_sinks.tf`

Reusable implementations cover centralized logging, CAI monitoring, network setup, and service controls in `1-org/modules/centralized-logging/main.tf`, `1-org/modules/cai-monitoring/main.tf`, and `1-org/modules/service_control/main.tf`.

## 2. Environment baselines
Development, nonproduction, and production are separate Terraform states and roots. Each creates its environment folder plus shared KMS and Secret Manager resources, consuming prior-stage organization outputs through remote-state configuration.
- `2-environments/envs/development/main.tf`
- `2-environments/envs/nonproduction/main.tf`
- `2-environments/modules/env_baseline/kms.tf`

## 3. Network architecture alternatives
Choose one mutually alternative stage-3 topology: conventional Shared VPC (`3-networks-svpc/`) or hub-and-spoke (`3-networks-hub-and-spoke/`). Each has `shared` plus per-environment roots, remote-state inputs, and outputs for downstream service projects.

Shared VPC modules establish VPCs, DNS, firewall, NAT, Private Service Connect, and private service access:
- `3-networks-svpc/modules/shared_vpc/main.tf`
- `3-networks-svpc/modules/shared_vpc/firewall.tf`
- `3-networks-hub-and-spoke/modules/shared_vpc/private_service_connect.tf`

Hub-and-spoke additionally models hubs, transitivity, HA VPN, and Dedicated/Partner Interconnect:
- `3-networks-hub-and-spoke/envs/shared/net-hubs.tf`
- `3-networks-hub-and-spoke/modules/transitivity/main.tf`
- `3-networks-hub-and-spoke/modules/vpn-ha/main.tf`

## 4. Business-unit service projects and pipeline delegation
Stage 4 creates business-unit folders and service projects per environment, attaching eligible projects to the selected Shared VPC. It also creates infrastructure-pipeline projects, separating platform-foundation deployment from application-infrastructure deployment.
- `4-projects/modules/base_env/business_unit_folder.tf`
- `4-projects/modules/single_project/main.tf`
- `4-projects/modules/infra_pipelines/main.tf`

The example roots are under `4-projects/business_unit_1/{shared,development,nonproduction,production}/`; these are intended to be replicated/customized for actual business units.

## 5. Application infrastructure workload layer
Stage 5 is the downstream consumer of the foundation: environment roots deploy application-facing infrastructure into the projects created in stage 4. The included example centers on a Compute Engine workload and supports Confidential Space resources.
- `5-app-infra/business_unit_1/development/main.tf`
- `5-app-infra/modules/env_base/main.tf`
- `5-app-infra/modules/confidential_space/main.tf`

## CI/CD, policy, and runtime boundaries
Terraform runs through Cloud Build, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Terraform Cloud patterns; scripts wrap plan/apply and authentication. Cloud Build definitions encode plan/apply workflows, while protected environment branches constrain deployment scope.
- `build/cloudbuild-tf-plan.yaml`
- `build/cloudbuild-tf-apply.yaml`
- `build/tf-wrapper.sh`

Plans are policy-validated with `gcloud terraform-tools` against OPA/Rego policy-library templates and constraints:
- `policy-library/lib/constraints.rego`
- `policy-library/policies/templates/gcp_iam_allowed_bindings.yaml`
- `policy-library/policies/constraints/iam_deny_public.yaml`

A Go-based deployment helper orchestrates validation, vet, apply, and destroy stages and integrates with GCP, GitHub, and GitLab:
- `helpers/foundation-deployer/main.go`
- `helpers/foundation-deployer/stages/executor.go`
- `helpers/foundation-deployer/gcp/gcp.go`
